anoint: Rub or sprinkle oil on (especially in a religious ceremony); designate as if by religious rite
bilk: Cheat or defraud, especially of money owed
delineate: Describe, portray, or outline with precision; trace the shape of
diurnal: Active during the day; happening daily
Abbreviation of Latin 'exempli gratia'; meaning 'for example'
figurative: Not literal; based on metaphor or imagery; representing one thing in terms of another
grovel: Crawl or behave abjectly in submission or fear; humble oneself excessively
handwringing: Excessive expression of distress or worry, often without taking effective action
naive: Showing a lack of experience, judgment, or sophistication; innocent or credulous
neologism: A newly coined word or expression
nevertheless: In spite of that; notwithstanding; even so
parley: A conference or discussion, especially between enemies, about terms of truce or other matters
posit: Put forward as fact or as a basis for argument; assume the existence of
precis: A concise summary of a text or speech
quibble: Argue or raise objections about a trivial matter; a minor objection
rococo: Of an ornate 18th-century style in art and architecture marked by elaborate curves and gilding; overly elaborate
somatic: Of or relating to the body, as distinct from the mind
synchronous: Existing or occurring at the same time; happening together
usury: The practice of lending money at unreasonably high rates of interest
viscous: Having a thick, sticky consistency between solid and liquid
circuitous: Indirect, roundabout; not direct in route or method
cliche: An overused expression or idea that has lost its original impact
